execution_status: NOT EXECUTED. No arm has been run. Nothing in this artefact reports a measurement

supersedes.note: the drafted design embedded at next_experiment in the Q3 result. That artefact is published and cited and is NOT edited; this preregistration carries its design forward and is the authority from here

amendment.what_changed: added CROSS_TRACK_ERROR as a declared secondary outcome, plus the look-ahead-domain measure fraction_of_steps_within_lookahead_radius and a per-step terminal mechanism trace
amendment.reason: Q3 established that the terminal miss was dominated by lateral offset rather than by shortfall along the route: 0.932 m short along the route against 1.396 m to the side, whose hypotenuse reproduces the recorded 1.6787 m goal distance to 0.0000 m, with 69% of the squared miss lateral. Without this measure an arm could reach the goal and be read as evidence for a route-tracking mechanism that was never measured
amendment.is_it_fixing_the_protocol_or_rescuing_a_: fixing the protocol. It adds an observation channel before any arm runs. It cannot change which arm wins, because the primary outcome and every acceptance rule are untouched

single_factor.arm_A_control: the frozen implementation, nearest qualifying route vertex
single_factor.arm_B_treatment: arc-length interpolated look-ahead point at the same frozen look-ahead distance along the polyline

design_carried_forward_unchanged.primary_outcome: entry into the 0.20 m goal region before max_steps
existing_secondary_outcomes: mean absolute heading error to target
held_constant: route geometry and the seeded generator
the collision guard and the kinematic drive
explicitly_forbidden: changing cruise_v or the speed law
changing more than one factor in the same run
justified_by: the stop branch was never reachable, so the failure is in the approach
terminal route-progress ran at 0.99 of the rate the remaining budget required
the goal vertex was never entered within the look-ahead radius, so the tracker steered at a single distant point for 444 steps
the offline command field differs materially between the two target rules at the poses actually visited
design_carried_forward_unchanged.sample_count: unchanged: one trajectory per arm, as the drafted power note already specified

secondary_outcome_cross_track_error.purpose: quantify whether changing ONLY target selection -- current path-vertex target versus arc-length interpolated look-ahead target -- changes lateral tracking relative to the frozen planned route

definition.per_step: cross_track_error_t is the Euclidean lateral distance from the realised position at step t to the nearest valid projection of that position onto the frozen planned polyline
definition.projection_rule: for each polyline segment, clamp the parametric foot of the perpendicular to [0, 1] so the projection cannot fall off the segment, then take the segment giving the smallest distance. The clamp is what makes the projection valid at vertices and beyond the endpoints
definition.sign_convention: the signed value is the 2-D cross product of the unit segment direction with the offset vector; every summary statistic in this preregistration is taken on the ABSOLUTE value, so the sign convention cannot affect any reported number
definition.applied_to: every recorded realised pose in both arms
definition.MUST_NOT_SUBSTITUTE: distance to the active target vertex is NOT cross-track error and may not stand in for it. The two differ by metres in run_00001
definition.MUST_NOT_REPLAN: both arms are measured against the SAME frozen polyline. Measuring an arm against a route replanned for that arm would make the arms incomparable

instrument_pinned.reason: the same implementation and the same coordinate conventions must measure both arms; pinning by content hash makes a silent change to the instrument detectable

frozen_route_polyline.provenance: recovered in Q2 by lattice search and re-verified in Q3: a unique solution matching the stored path length to 3.6e-15 m

windows.whole_trajectory: every recorded step of the arm

terminal_planned_leg.definition: the arclength window from the last interior route vertex to the sealed goal, identical in both arms because it is a property of the frozen route and not of behaviour
terminal_planned_leg.note: the STEP at which each arm enters this window will differ between arms; the WINDOW does not. Comparisons are made over the window, not over a fixed step range

secondary_outcome_cross_track_error.threshold_status: NONE. These are descriptive. No pass/fail threshold is defined here, and none may be introduced after results are seen

historical_values_are_motivation_only.WARNING: these motivated the measurement. They are NOT a target, NOT a baseline to beat, and NOT a criterion. run_00001 is a different experiment: it is the observational run the intervention exists to follow up, not a control arm

secondary_outcome_lookahead_domain.name: fraction_of_steps_within_lookahead_radius
secondary_outcome_lookahead_domain.definition: count(absolute cross_track_error <= 0.45 m) divided by the number of valid recorded steps
secondary_outcome_lookahead_domain.radius_provenance: the frozen look-ahead already in the collection configuration. It is used here as a domain boundary, not as an acceptance threshold, and no new number was invented
secondary_outcome_lookahead_domain.INTERPRETATION_CAVEAT: cross_track <= lookahead_radius must NOT be read as proof that a textbook pure-pursuit circle intersection exists at that step. The circle of the look-ahead radius centred on the robot also requires enough path remaining ahead of the projection for a FORWARD intersection to exist, which fails near the end of a route. Claim a valid intersection only where both geometric preconditions are checked explicitly
secondary_outcome_lookahead_domain.why_it_is_worth_measuring: in run_00001 cross-track reached 2.589 m against a 0.45 m radius, so a circle-intersection tracker would have had no solution for most of the run. This measure says how much of each arm sits inside the geometry the look-ahead assumes

terminal_mechanism_trace.purpose: permit testing whether any difference in goal approach coincides with a difference in lateral tracking, rather than asserting it
terminal_mechanism_trace.format: one CSV per arm, committed as text evidence

interpretation_rules.primary_conclusion_source: the already-frozen primary outcome alone. Cross-track is secondary and may not carry the primary conclusion
interpretation_rules.allowed_phrasing: the interpolated-target arm was associated with lower or higher lateral tracking error
interpretation_rules.case_goal_improves_and_cross_track_impro: supports the hypothesis that improved route tracking is part of the observed mechanism. It does NOT by itself prove mediation
interpretation_rules.case_goal_improves_but_cross_track_does_: do NOT claim the benefit operated through lateral tracking
interpretation_rules.case_cross_track_improves_but_goal_does_: report improved tracking WITHOUT claiming improved task completion
interpretation_rules.case_neither_improves: report no observed improvement in this instance
interpretation_rules.mediation_requires: a design that varies the mediator, which this one-factor intervention does not

power_and_claim_limit.retained_from_the_draft: one trajectory per arm establishes a difference in one instance, not a difference in expectation. A route population and a seed sweep are required before any success-rate claim, and that is a separate design
power_and_claim_limit.may_demonstrate: a difference in this controlled instance, with every other factor held constant
may_not_demonstrate: that the physical robot would behave similarly
power_and_claim_limit.NO_SIGNIFICANCE_TESTING: statistical significance must not be reported from one trajectory per arm. No p-value, no confidence interval, no significance claim
power_and_claim_limit.what_a_population_claim_would_need: a route population and a seed sweep, preregistered separately
